title: Living faith and repentance required, yet not meritorious
source_text: XVI. Praeterea fatendum est Deum, ut nobis Christi satisfactionem & meritum imputet, & propter Christum nos peccatorum venia & filiorum adoptione donet, istud a nobis exigere, ut in Christum fide viva & efficaci credamus, veramque & seriam peccatorum nostrorum poenitentiam agamus. Nec enim deceret Dei sapientiam peccata remittere illis qui obstinate in peccatis perseverare volunt, & gratiae ac salutis participes facere illos qui Christi gratiam aspernantur, eumque tanquam Servatorem & Redemptorem suum, uti par est, agnoscere & colere recusant. Sed ne fides & poenitentia sint conditio quaedam a Deo praerequisita ut beneficium istud ab eo accipiamus, & sine qua non convenit nos ejus fieri compotes; nec fides tamen, nec poenitentia remissionem peccatorum & adoptionem filiorum merentur; neque causae sunt propter quam, & cujus dignitate, merito, & efficacia, tam eximiam gratiam consequimur. Sed tota & in solidum ad Christi obedientiam & meritum est referenda: quantum vero nos spectat simpliciter, & omni ex parte gratuita est, nec ullis nostris actibus, sive operibus, debetur.
pass_a_gloss: Further it must be confessed that God, in order to impute to us Christ’s satisfaction and merit and for Christ’s sake to gift us with pardon of sins and adoption of sons, requires of us that we believe in Christ with living and efficacious faith and enact true and serious repentance of our sins. For it would not befit God’s wisdom to remit sins to those who obstinately will to persevere in sins, and to make sharers of grace and salvation those who spurn Christ’s grace and refuse to acknowledge and honor him as their Savior and Redeemer as is fitting. But though faith and repentance are a certain condition God requires beforehand so that we receive that benefit from him, and without which it is not fitting that we become partakers of it, yet neither faith nor repentance merits the remission of sins and the adoption of sons; nor are they causes on account of which, and by whose dignity, merit, and efficacy, we obtain so excellent a grace. Rather the whole is referred wholly and solidly to Christ’s obedience and merit: as for us it is simply and in every respect gratuitous, and is owed to none of our acts or works.
pass_b_english: God requires living faith and serious repentance before imputing Christ’s merit.
Those acts are prerequisite conditions, not meritorious causes—grace remains wholly free for Christ’s sake.
